scenes.title: THE SKY REMEMBERS.
lines: Khonsu takes its name from the Egyptian lunar deity, the traveler.
The sky-rewinding moment in Moon Knight inspired us to turn wonder into an instrument for exploring time.
Our artwork is original. Our observation dates come from the telescope.

scenes.title: ENTER THE OBSERVATORY
lines: Built by ByteBoyz, Khonsu makes the infrared sky approachable for curious people, not only specialists.
Choose Explore the Sky. A short, skippable introduction brings you into the console while observations load.

audio.text: Built by ByteBoyz, Khonsu makes the infrared sky approachable for curious people, not only specialists.

scenes.title: CHOOSE YOUR PATCH
lines: In Field, enter right ascension and declination in degrees, then choose the field of view in arcminutes.
The named presets fill coordinates for the five challenge targets. Search this field starts a bounded archive request.
This walkthrough uses the saved WISE 0855 field: genuine SPHEREx data, not a live search or simulated stars.

scenes.title: ONE SKY. MANY MOMENTS.
lines: Drag the amber time dial or use Previous and Next to step between actual observation dates.
The handle follows your pointer and springs to a real epoch when released. Play advances through the available frames.
Unequal time gaps stay visible. We do not invent observations between visits.

scenes.title: LOOK CLOSER
lines: Fit shows the whole observed field. Fill uses more of the console by cropping the view.
Choose Pan to move around, and zoom in for inspection. The sky keeps its original geometry.
Keyboard controls offer another way to move through time and explore the image.

scenes.title: PAUSE. COMPARE. NOTICE.
lines: Use Compare to choose observations A and B. Blink alternates them, while Hold for B gives a temporary comparison.
Read their dates and wavelengths before interpreting a difference. Noise, changing backgrounds and unmatched blur can mimic change.

scenes.title: A CLEARER VIEW
lines: Clean View estimates eligible missing patches to make the image easier to explore.
Show original returns to measured data. Estimated-area highlighting reveals where visual guesses were used.
Advanced controls adjust presentation and display resolution. More screen pixels cannot create finer telescope measurements.

scenes.title: ASK WHAT A PIXEL MEANS
lines: In Layers, turn on the quality overlay and choose Inspect to understand a pixel.
Warning samples, missing measurements and estimated areas remain distinct. Hiding a layer does not repair the data.
Info preserves the actual dates, source identifiers, release, wavelength and processing context.

scenes.title: PUT THE SKY IN CONTEXT
lines: Optional Gaia markers provide known-source context. The separate WISE reference pane offers another telescope view.
These depend on external services. An unmarked point is not automatically a new object, and an overlay is not a confirmed match.

audio.text: Optional Gaia markers provide known-source context. The separate WISE reference pane offers another telescope view.

scenes.title: KEEP YOUR OBSERVATIONS
lines: Open Notes and write what you notice. You can save an observation note without marking a pixel.
Edit, delete or export your notes. A sequence and its displayed observation are attached when available.
The browser keeps a copy. Configured local Docker storage adds a private SQLite backup, with clear offline and conflict feedback.

scenes.title: FROM CURIOSITY TO EVIDENCE
lines: For a specific position, choose Mark, select the image, and save a candidate note.
The evidence retains its position, original validity, observation dates, comparison context and source references.
Export downloads a portable record. A candidate is a question to investigate, not a confirmed discovery.

scenes.title: SHARE THE FIELD
lines: Share creates a coordinate link without private notes. Opening it fills the search, rather than silently downloading archive data.
Guided Mode walks through the controls. The Docs page explains features, testing, image limitations and notebook recovery.
